sections.html: Casa Grande is a Pinal County city roughly halfway between Phoenix and Tucson, using the ZIP codes 85122, 85130, 85193 and 85194. The population estimate for July 1, 2025 is 69,753, which is 29.9% above the April 2020 base of 53,705. Most working residents commute toward the Phoenix area or toward Tucson, with a mean trip of 23.3 minutes. New jobs bring new renters and first-time buyers and also bring new construction, so an older house will be compared with recently built homes nearby.

Casa Grande is mostly owner-occupied, with a median home value near $304,000 for 2020 to 2024.

The City of Casa Grande Building Division issues permits for construction, alteration, repair, installation, demolition and occupancy-related work. The city lists additions, remodeling, structural work, pools and spas, solar systems, accessory structures and mechanical, electrical, plumbing or gas work as common permit projects, and the Building Division makes the final call. If you're unsure, contact the Development Center before starting. The Building Division is at 510 E. Florence Blvd and answers at 520-421-8630.

If a previous owner added a room, a patio cover or a pool, ask the Building Division for the permit record before you list or accept an offer. Finished work should have a passed final inspection, and a building should not be occupied until any required certificate of occupancy is issued. Heat is hard on roofs, cooling systems and exterior finishes, and a buyer's inspector is likely to check them, so know their age.

A landlord who rented a house short term and now wants to sell should know the city's ordinance, No. 1397.05.06, which took effect January 1, 2025. State law at A.R.S. 9-500.39 allows short-term rentals in every Arizona city, so Casa Grande regulates them through a permit instead of banning them. An owner's steps are:

  • Get a Transaction Privilege Tax license from the Arizona Department of Revenue.
  • Notify the Pinal County Assessor's Office of the rental status.
  • Apply for the city permit, which costs $115 and renews annually for $115.
  • Notify neighbors next door and across the street, and file the attestation within seven business days of getting the permit.
  • Post the owner and emergency contact where guests can see it.

Operating without a permit can bring civil penalties of up to $1,000 for every 30 days after a 30-day notice. Rules and fees change, so read the city's short-term rental page before relying on these figures.

sections.h2: Deed, recording and property tax in a Casa Grande sale
sections.html:
A Casa Grande sale is recorded with the Pinal County Recorder, and the standard recording fee is $30 per document. The fee schedule, effective July 1, 2019, folds in the affidavit of property value, extra indexing and a $1 charge for mailing the document back.

A.R.S. 11-1133 requires each deed to carry an affidavit of legal value signed by the buyer and seller or their agents. It states the sale price, the date, the parcel number and whether the buyer will occupy or rent the home. The recorder must refuse a deed without a complete affidavit unless the deed notes an exemption under A.R.S. 11-1134, such as a deed of gift or a conveyance made under a court order. Your title or escrow company normally prepares this paperwork.

On Pinal County parcels, a tax bill over $100 is paid in two halves. The first half is due October 1 and delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 1, and the second half is due March 1 and delinquent after 5 p.m. on May 1. When the date falls on a weekend or holiday, delinquency moves to the next business day, and late interest runs at 16% a year, prorated monthly.

Ask the Pinal County Treasurer for a payoff that includes any prior-year taxes and interest, and give the number to the title company before the contract is signed. An owner who lets a tax installment slide still has to clear it at closing, so the cash you receive is the price minus that balance and any loan payoff.

A cash sale doesn't change that math. It only removes the lender's appraisal and underwriting from the timeline, because the buyer isn't borrowing.

sections.h2: How a Casa Grande closing goes
sections.html: Once you accept an offer, the title or escrow company opens the file, orders the payoff figures and prepares the deed and the affidavit. You sign the deed, and the company records it with the Pinal County Recorder and pays you from the proceeds. Before you reach that stage, line up the permit record for any addition, pool or solar work, and if you rented short term, close out the city permit and the state license. Tell the Pinal County Assessor's Office when the rental status changes.

faqs.q: How many people live in Casa Grande?
faqs.a: The estimate is 69,753 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 53,705 in April 2020. The city sits in Pinal County between Phoenix and Tucson.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Casa Grande?
faqs.a: The Pinal County Recorder charges $30 for most documents, including a deed, and the fee covers the affidavit of property value and return postage. Your title or escrow company usually pays it at closing.

faqs.q: Does a Casa Grande rental need a city permit?
faqs.a: Yes, any property rented for less than 30 days needs a Casa Grande Short-Term Rental Permit, which costs $115 a year. Owners also need a state Transaction Privilege Tax license and must notify the Pinal County Assessor and nearby neighbors.

faqs.q: When are Pinal County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes over $100 are due in halves, October 1 and March 1, and become delinquent after 5 p.m. on the following November 1 and May 1. Late payments accrue 16% simple interest per year, prorated monthly.

faqs.q: Who do I call about permits for work done on my Casa Grande house?
faqs.a: The Building Division, at 510 E. Florence Blvd or 520-421-8630. Ask for the permit record on any addition, pool or solar system before you list.
